title: fix(v4): make fromJSONSchema propertyNames compose with the other object keywords
body:
Closes #6323. Includes #6327 — @deepshekhardas's commits are in this branch, so merging here lands their fix too.

`propertyNames` was modelled as a record, which short-circuited the whole object branch: the `patternProperties` and `additionalProperties` handling below it never ran. That conflated a constraint on key *names* with one on values, and silently dropped three keywords.

```ts
z.fromJSONSchema({
  type: "object",
  properties: { a: { type: "number" } },
  propertyNames: { enum: ["a", "b"] },
  additionalProperties: { type: "string" },
}).parse({ a: 1 });
// before: ✖ invalid_type at ["a"] — additionalProperties was applied to a
//            key that `properties` declares
// after:  ✔
```

Same cause, two more symptoms: `additionalProperties: false` and `patternProperties` were both ignored whenever `propertyNames` was present, because the branch only read `additionalProperties` when it happened to be an object schema.

`propertyNames` is now a key guard that runs ahead of the object parse, so all four keywords compose. It has to see the raw input rather than the parsed object — an object parse drops `__proto__`, and a property `default` adds keys the instance never carried, so the parsed output is not the set of names to validate. The guard is an identity transform rather than `z.any()` so `toJSONSchema` still reports the object on the input side of the pipe as well as the output side.

`toJSONSchema` can't infer that guard, so the original keyword rides along as metadata — the round trip stays lossless in both `io` modes and now reproduces the source keyword verbatim (`{ enum: [...] }`) instead of the record-derived `{ type: "string", enum: [...] }`. The metadata is attached only where the guard applies: not on a non-object type, and not on a `$ref`, where it would land on the target every reference shares.

Three smaller `propertyNames` fixes fall out of the same rewrite:

- `propertyNames: false` is enforced instead of ignored; `true` skips the guard.
- A subschema that omits `type` now constrains keys instead of converting to `z.any()`. Keys are always strings, so `{ "pattern": "^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$" }` — the spelling json-schema.org's own example uses — was previously a complete no-op.
- `__proto__` is rejected rather than silently dropped.

Not addressed here: a `required` array naming keys that `properties` never declares is still ignored. I had it in an earlier pass, but injecting those keys into the shape makes `additionalProperties` override a `patternProperties` match and makes `additionalProperties: false` accept a key it forbids, so it needs its own change.

reviews.body: Copilot was unable to review this pull request because the user who requested the review has reached their quota limit.

> ℹ️ Two rough edges worth a look — the core restructuring is sound. **Reviewed changes** — the rewritten `case "object"` branch of `from-json-schema.ts` and its eight new tests, checked against the JSON Schema draft-2020-12 object keywords and against Zod's own `$ZodRecord` issue construction. - **`propertyNames` demoted to a post-hoc check** — `checkPropertyNames` (new lines 146-164) layers a `.check()` over whatever `properties` / `patternProperties` / `additionalProperties` produced, replacing the record/intersection modelling that `break`-ed early and swallowed the sibling keywords. - **`additionalProperties` hoisted to `additionalSchema`** (new lines 398-401) so the `required` fallback and the `else` branch share one conversion. - **`required` keys absent from `properties`** now enter the shape with `additionalSchema ?? z.any()` (new lines 410-414) instead of being dropped. - **`propertyNames` copied into `extraMeta`** (new lines 623-627) to keep the round trip lossless. Worth noting this is load-bearing, not redundant: `propertyNames` is in `RECOGNIZED_KEYS`, so the generic fallthrough loop would otherwise drop it. I ran the suite (80 tests in `from-json-schema.test.ts`, plus `to-json-schema.test.ts`) and spot-checked that the new tests actually fail against the old modelling rather than passing incidentally — the `additionalProperties: false` and `patternProperties` combos are genuine regression coverage. The issue shape `checkPropertyNames` pushes matches `$ZodRecord`'s own `invalid_key` at `core/schemas.ts:2905`, and `prettifyError` / `treeifyError` render it correctly. ### ℹ️ `additionalProperties` still doesn't compose with `patternProperties` The PR body says `propertyNames` is layered on "so all four compose", but one pairing remains broken. The new `else` at line 450 preserves the old `break` at old-line 440 exactly, so `additionalProperties` is never consulted when `patternProperties` is present. Confirmed: `{ type: "object", patternProperties: { "^S_": { type: "string" } }, additionalProperties: false }` accepts `{ other: "x" }`, which the spec says must fail. This is pre-existing and faithfully preserved by the refactor, so it's not a regression — flagging only because the PR's framing implies otherwise, and because the restructure is the natural moment to decide whether to close it or leave it documented.
Technical details ````markdown # `additionalProperties` is unreachable when `patternProperties` is set ## Affected sites - `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/from-json-schema.ts:417-465` — `if (schema.patternProperties) { ... } else { /* additionalProperties */ }`. The `else` means the two keywords are mutually exclusive, but the spec composes them. ## Spec behavior `additionalProperties` applies to instance properties matched by neither `properties` nor `patternProperties` (https://www.learnjsonschema.com/2020-12/applicator/additionalproperties/). Today those keys fall through the `z.looseRecord`s built at line 427 unvalidated. ## Required outcome Either enforce `additionalProperties` alongside `patternProperties`, or reword the PR body so it doesn't claim all four keywords compose. ## Suggested approach (optional) The `patternProperties` branch already needs a post-check to express strictness (`z.looseRecord` intentionally passes non-matching keys through). The same mechanism `checkPropertyNames` introduces could carry it: after building the intersection, add a check that issues `unrecognized_keys` for keys matched by neither `properties` nor any compiled pattern regex when `additionalProperties === false`, or validates them against `additionalSchema` when it is a schema. ## Open questions for the human - Is closing this in-scope here, or is it better as a follow-up so this PR stays focused on `propertyNames`? ````
### ℹ️ Nitpicks - A `propertyNames` subschema without `"type": "string"` converts to `z.any()`, so the constraint is dropped entirely. Since property names are strings by definition, `propertyNames: { pattern: "^S_" }` is the idiomatic spelling — and it silently validates nothing. The new test at `from-json-schema.test.ts:406` sidesteps this by writing `type: "string", pattern: "^S_"`. Pre-existing, but it does limit how much of this fix real-world schemas will reach. - `required: ["a"]` with `additionalProperties: false` and no matching `properties` entry is unsatisfiable per spec. The new fallback gives it `z.any()`, which lands it in the shape and so exempts it from `.strict()` — `{ a: "x" }` now parses where it previously threw. The old code had the mirror-image bug (`{}` passed), so this isn't a clean regression, just a note that neither revision gets the pathological case right.   ｜ [Fix all ➔](https://pullfrog.com/trigger/colinhacks/zod/6411?action=fix&review_id=4933153545) ｜ [Fix 👍s ➔](https://pullfrog.com/trigger/colinhacks/zod/6411?action=fix-approved&review_id=4933153545) ｜ [View workflow run](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/actions/runs/31761700950/job/94649256969) ｜ Using `Claude Opus` ｜ [𝕏](https://x.com/pullfrogai)

> [!IMPORTANT] > The move to a piped guard fixes the two things I flagged last round, but the `z.transform` on the input side has two consequences the tests don't reach — including one that breaks the losslessness claim in the PR body. **Reviewed changes** — the delta from `9341d89` to `9bf1a42`, which reworks how the `propertyNames` guard is attached and drops the `required` fallback. - **Guard moved ahead of the object parse** — `checkPropertyNames` no longer `.check()`s the parsed value; it builds `z.transform((v) => v).check(...)` and returns `guard.pipe(objectSchema)` so the check sees raw input. The `__proto__` and `default`-synthesized-key motivations both check out, and the two new tests genuinely fail against the old design. - **`required` fallback removed** — the loop that injected undeclared `required` keys into `shape` is gone, and the gap is now stated in the PR body instead. That retires my previous comment on the `key in shape` prototype collision. - **`propertyNames: false` now enforced** — the guard is `!== undefined && !== true`, with coverage in the new `boolean propertyNames` test. - **Typeless subschemas get a synthetic `type: "string"`** — so `{ pattern: "..." }` constrains keys instead of converting to `z.any()`. - **Metadata narrowed** — `extraMeta.propertyNames` is now gated on `type === "object" && $ref === undefined`, with a test asserting it doesn't leak onto a shared `$ref` target. I re-ran `from-json-schema.test.ts` (83) and `to-json-schema.test.ts` (79) — all green, typecheck clean. ### ℹ️ Nitpicks - `Object.getOwnPropertyNames` (line 160) isn't needed for the reason the doc comment gives. `Object.keys` already returns `["__proto__"]` for a `JSON.parse('{"__proto__":1}')` result — `JSON.parse` creates it as an own *enumerable* data property. The only behavioral difference is that non-enumerable own properties are now validated as key names, which nothing else in the object parse looks at. `Object.keys` matches what `$ZodRecord` uses. - The pipe short-circuits, so a bad key name now suppresses every value error. `handlePipeResult` (`core/schemas.ts:4038`) sets `aborted = true` whenever the left side has issues, `continue: true` or not — `{ a: "not a number", zzz: "bad key" }` on `{ properties: { a: { type: "number" } }, propertyNames: { enum: ["a"] }, additionalProperties: { type: "string" } }` reports only `invalid_key` at `["zzz"]`. That's the mirror image of the old design (where a failed object parse hid the key issues), so it's a sideways move rather than a regression, but the PR body's acknowledgement of the old direction is now stale. - The `type: "string"` injection is one level deep, so the comment at line 476 overstates slightly. Members inside a composition keyword are converted independently and still hit the typeless `z.any()` fallback: `propertyNames: { oneOf: [{ pattern: "^a" }, { pattern: "^b" }] }` rejects *every* key (two `z.any()` branches both match, so `z.xor` never succeeds), and `propertyNames: { allOf: [{ pattern: "^a" }, { minLength: 3 }] }` accepts every key. Pre-existing and general — `fromJSONSchema({ oneOf: [{ pattern: "^a" }] })` fails the same way with no object in sight — so not something this PR has to fix, just worth not claiming. - Typo at line 637: "the shared target shared by every reference".   ｜ [Fix all ➔](https://pullfrog.com/trigger/colinhacks/zod/6411?action=fix&review_id=4933249456) ｜ [Fix 👍s ➔](https://pullfrog.com/trigger/colinhacks/zod/6411?action=fix-approved&review_id=4933249456) ｜ [View workflow run](https://github.com/colinhacks/zod/actions/runs/31763083831/job/94653334858) ｜ Using `Claude Opus` ｜ [𝕏](https://x.com/pullfrogai)

This guard is truthiness-based while the new metadata block at line 625 uses `!== undefined`, so `propertyNames: false` gets emitted into the round-tripped JSON Schema without ever being enforced — the resulting Zod schema accepts every key. `propertyNames` is typed `_JSONSchema = boolean | JSONSchema`, so `false` is a legal input, and `convertSchema` already handles boolean schemas (`fromJSONSchema(false)` yields a rejecting schema), so tightening the guard makes the `false` case work rather than merely aligning the two conditions.

`$ZodTransform` sets `_zod.optin = "optional"` (`core/schemas.ts:3425`) and `$ZodPipe` inherits `optin` from `def.in` (`core/schemas.ts:4017`), so every guarded object now advertises itself as optional-on-input. `objectProcessor` computes `required` as `optin === undefined` for `io: "input"` (`core/json-schema-processors.ts:310`), which means a guarded object nested as a property silently drops out of its parent's `required` array — the losslessness the PR body claims for both `io` modes holds only at the top level, which is the only place the new test loop looks.

The same transform also makes the schema unencodable: `$ZodTransform._zod.parse` throws `$ZodEncodeError` in the backward direction (`core/schemas.ts:3427`), so `z.encode` now fails on any object carrying `propertyNames`.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# The identity transform leaks `optin: "optional"` and blocks `encode`

## Affected sites
- `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/from-json-schema.ts:155-156` — `z.transform((value: unknown) => value)` is the in-side of the pipe returned at line 173. `$ZodTransform` hardcodes `optin = "optional"` and throws on `direction === "backward"`.
- `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/tests/from-json-schema.test.ts:470-484` — the `io` loop only converts a top-level guarded object, where the parent-`required` computation never runs.

## Reproductions
```ts
const src = {
  type: "object",
  properties: { a: { type: "object", propertyNames: { enum: ["x"] } } },
  required: ["a"],
};
z.toJSONSchema(fromJSONSchema(src), { io: "input" }).required; // undefined
// drop `propertyNames` from the inner schema and it is ["a"]
// io: "output" is unaffected — `optout` comes from `def.out`

const enc = fromJSONSchema({
  type: "object",
  properties: { a: { type: "string" } },
  propertyNames: { enum: ["a"] },
});
z.encode(enc, { a: "x" });
// $ZodEncodeError: Encountered unidirectional transform during encode: ZodTransform
// the same schema without `propertyNames` encodes fine
```

Runtime requiredness is NOT affected — `util.optionalKeys` requires both `optin` and `optout` to be `"optional"`, and `optout` still comes from the object. This is purely a `toJSONSchema` and `encode` problem.

## Required outcome
- A guarded object nested under `required` keeps its place in the parent's `required` array for `io: "input"`.
- Either `encode` keeps working through a guarded object, or the limitation is a deliberate, stated trade-off.
- Whichever way it lands, the `io` loop should cover a *nested* guarded object, since the top-level case cannot catch either issue.

## Suggested approach (optional)
The transform is load-bearing for representation — `pipeProcessor` (`core/json-schema-processors.ts:531-532`) special-cases `def.in._zod.traits.has("$ZodTransform")` to emit `def.out` for `io: "input"`, so swapping in `z.any()` or `z.unknown()` would make `io: "input"` report the guard instead of the object. Two directions that keep it:
- Fix `objectProcessor` to read declared optionality off `def.out` for transform-fronted pipes rather than the runtime `optin` flag. That is the more general fix and helps every hand-rolled `z.pipe(z.transform(...), obj)`, but it is a core change and widens this PR considerably.
- Or keep the change local: build the guard as a `z.codec` whose reverse transform is also the identity, which is bidirectional and gives you a place to control `optin`.

## Open questions for the human
- Is `z.encode` on `fromJSONSchema` output a use case you want to hold, or is `fromJSONSchema` decode-only by contract? That answer decides whether the second half of this is a bug or a documented limitation.
````

</details>

inline.body:
With the `required` fallback gone, `additionalSchema` has exactly one consumer left (line 462), inside the `else` that only runs when `patternProperties` is absent — but it is still computed unconditionally. That turns a previously-lazy conversion into an eager one, so a schema whose `additionalProperties` was harmlessly ignored can now throw during conversion.

<details><summary>Technical details</summary>

````markdown
# Hoisted `additionalSchema` converts a subschema the branch never uses

## Affected sites
- `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/from-json-schema.ts:408-411` — computed before the `patternProperties` / `else` split.
- `packages/zod/src/v4/classic/from-json-schema.ts:462-464` — the only remaining read.

## Reproduction
```ts
fromJSONSchema({
  type: "object",
  patternProperties: { "^S_": { type: "string" } },
  additionalProperties: { not: { type: "string" } },
});
// throws: not is not supported in Zod (except { not: {} } for never)
// on main this converts fine — additionalProperties is ignored when
// patternProperties is present, so it was never converted
```
`convertSchema` also mutates `ctx` (refs, registry), so the eager call has side effects for a schema that is then discarded.

## Required outcome
`additionalProperties` is converted only on the path that consumes it, restoring the previous behavior for the `patternProperties` combination.

## Suggested approach (optional)
Delete lines 408-411 and put the conversion back inline at line 464: `zodSchema = objectSchema.catchall(convertSchema(schema.additionalProperties as JSONSchema.JSONSchema, ctx));`, with the guard at 462 back to `typeof schema.additionalProperties === "object"`.
````

</details>
